status: review-only; not wired into the build
policy: Records omitted from this file are deliberate keeps from the source-audited translation.

changes.TT5/g0/r0: Man: We're free! We're finally free! Long live Lincoln!
changes.TT5/g0/r1: Lincoln: Government of the people, by the people, for the people must endure! America must be a nation of freedom and equality!
changes.TT5/g0/r2: Belle: Thank you, sir. Meyer: This puts me in quite a bind… I don't know how I'll run the farm without you. Belle: Please, sir… we've dreamed of freedom for so long. Meyer: I understand. I'll miss you. Finish the work that's left, and then you're free to go. Belle: Thank you!
changes.TT5/g0/r3: Meyer: You've worked hard. It's already late, so leave tomorrow morning instead. Belle: Yes, sir.
changes.TT5/g0/r4: Voice: Thank you for bringing us safely through another day. Amen. Good night, George. George: Good night.
changes.TT5/g0/r5: But the day wasn't over yet…
changes.TT5/g0/r6: Man: Emancipation?! Don't start getting ideas around here! Here's an example of what happens when you do—taste my whip!
changes.TT5/g0/r7: Crack! Me: Aaaaagh! Belle: Please, sir! You'll kill my son! Man: Listen well, George! Me: … Man: You were born a slave. Lincoln can say whatever he likes. As long as you're here, there is no freedom. Remember that!
changes.TT5/g0/r8: His face is twisted in pain.
changes.TT5/g0/r10: She pleads with him through tears.
changes.TT5/g0/r11: In the torchlight, the mask looks even more sinister.
changes.TT5/g0/r16: Man: Boss! Look what I found. Man: A hundred-dollar bill! Belle: Th-that money… Man: You don't need it. I'll hold on to it for you. Belle: You demon! You devil! Man: Shut up!
changes.TT5/g0/r18: Man: Stay in the South. Spend your lives working for us. Understand…?
changes.TT5/g0/r21: We don't have a home anymore.
changes.TT5/g0/r27: The bills are dirty and badly wrinkled. Belle: That's our blood and sweat.
changes.TT5/g0/r30: Belle: At this hour…? Eek! Me: W-who are you? Man: I'm here to teach you the cold facts of life…
changes.TT5/g0/r31: Belle: You're free now. You don't have to work yourself to the bone anymore. Me: Um… who are you? Belle: What's gotten into you? Don't tease your mother.
changes.TT5/g1/r0: Belle: Our friends left one by one. Now it's just us and old Tom, with more work than ever.
changes.TT5/g1/r1: Belle: It's time we left this place. Me: … Belle: Master Meyer isn't like most men in the South. I'm sure he'll let us go.
changes.TT5/g1/r4: Belle: Don't take that! I've been saving it for decades. That money means everything to me.
changes.TT5/g1/r6: TIME: SEPTEMBER 1864 — PLACE: ATLANTA, UNITED STATES — NAME: GEORGE — OCCUPATION: FARMHAND ON MEYER'S FARM
changes.TT5/g1/r9: Be strong, George! Are you all right?! George!
changes.TT5/g1/r10: My head is swimming… My whole body feels heavy. And my throat is bone-dry. Belle: George! Meyer: Mild sunstroke. Let him sleep. He'll recover.
changes.TT5/g1/r13: George: Lincoln is still out there. That means we still have a future. He's a child of God.
changes.TT5/g1/r14: George: It's all right, Mom. It's my job.
changes.TT5/g1/r16: Meyer: Get to work. If you want to finish efficiently, you need to do the jobs in the proper order.
changes.TT5/g1/r17: Meyer: Listen carefully, then do exactly as I tell you.
changes.TT5/g1/r18: Meyer: Lose track of the order and you'll never finish today.
changes.TT5/g1/r19: Meyer: Pick cotton and fill twenty-eight five-kilogram baskets. Cut 120 logs, each seventy centimeters long. Rest for ten minutes. Then fetch water from the stream: two buckets per trip, three trips. Weed for one hour. Rest for fifteen minutes. Finally, repair four damaged spots on the mansion roof.
changes.TT5/g1/r21: Meyer: I'm busy. I'll repeat it once more, and only once.
changes.TT5/g1/r26: All right! Let's get to it!
changes.TT5/g1/r29: Meyer: There you are. Me: I finished everything. Meyer: Tom is falling behind. He's by the livestock shed. Go give him a hand. Me: …
changes.TT5/g2/r3: Tom: Belle! Perfect timing! This problem makes no sense to me, and I'm stuck.
changes.TT5/g2/r7: The bills are dirty and wrinkled. Me: These bills… Tom: Got paid this morning. Me: …
changes.TT5/g2/r8: Tom: The livestock trader will be here soon. Thanks to George, we'll finally be able to buy some animals. Good news!
changes.TT5/g2/r9: Tom: Belle, help him close the deal quickly.
changes.TT5/g2/r10: Tom: My eyes aren't what they used to be. Mind counting this for me? It's a bundle of hundred-dollar bills.
changes.TT5/g2/r11: Trader: Say… know the answer to this one?
changes.TT5/g2/r12: Who fought Native Americans to protect white settlers?
changes.TT5/g2/r15: What American fleet forced Japan to open its ports?
changes.TT5/g2/r16: Who wrote the novel said to have helped spark the Civil War, "Uncle Tom's Cabin"?
changes.TT5/g2/r17: What South Dakota mountain bears the faces of four presidents?
changes.TT5/g2/r18: Along with the phonograph and generator, what was considered one of Edison's three great inventions?
changes.TT5/g2/r19: Trader: Correct! Every answer! Well done. Now, let's do business.
changes.TT5/g2/r20: Time softens every sorrow. An old American proverb.
changes.TT5/g2/r22: Tom: George! Finally! I need your help with something.
changes.TT5/g2/r23: Tom: I have exactly one thousand dollars. I need to buy fifty animals total—cows, sheep, and pigs. Cows cost $120 each, sheep $30, and pigs $5. How many of each should I buy?
changes.TT5/g2/r24: Tom: That's it! Perfect! Now I can buy them.
changes.TT5/g2/r25: Tom: Master! Good news! I finally solved it! Meyer: Well done, Tom. George… Me: Yes…? Meyer: Belle needs help. Go give her a hand in the kitchen.
changes.TT5/g2/r28: Belle: There are three bottles. The one-liter bottle is empty. The 500-milliliter and 300-milliliter bottles are full of milk. Master Meyer says…
changes.TT5/g2/r29: Belle: He wants exactly 700 milliliters in the one-liter bottle. None of them have markings… Please help me figure it out.
changes.TT5/g3/r12: Belle: We did it! All the work is finished. We're finally free! We can leave the South!
changes.TT5/g3/r13: Meyer: Those miserable people… Don't lose heart, Belle. Stay here, work, and save your money again. Me: …
changes.TT5/g3/r16: Meyer: I'll be back by noon with a special guest. I don't want any mistakes. A friend of mine is preparing the reception. Stay out of the manor until then.
changes.TT5/g3/r19: There's a cave in the distance, with light spilling out.
changes.TT5/g3/r20: The river flows gently. I can hear faint voices carrying over the water.
changes.TT5/g3/r23: A hand poised to seize something… I've seen this before.
changes.TT5/g3/r24: They're chanting dark incantations toward the altar.
changes.TT5/g3/r25: Man: We've made pacts with the Devil. Now we fear nothing. We'll make the dark history the Devil dreams of a reality!
